opening_message:
Ticket 1: Keith Mclaughlin (employee ID E032) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E032.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Keith Mclaughlin is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, max is write (Source Code is owned by Engineer, so no admin). Grant write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Keith Mclaughlin is a contractor with basic security training (note claiming full-time appears incorrect). Contractors need advanced training for write; max is read. Requested write, so recommend granting read.
reason: Requested write access to Source Code. HR note claims full-time (max write), but Security DB (which looked up employment type and security training) shows Keith Mclaughlin is a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training, and never admin. Since the employee is a contractor with only basic training, the maximum is read. The requested write exceeds the maximum, so grant read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket carefully.

The employee Keith Mclaughlin (E032) requests write access to Source Code.

Two notes:
- HR agent: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation write. Says full-time employee max is write (Source Code owned by Engineer, so no admin). Grant write.
- Security agent: role Analyst (not looked up), employment type contractor (looked up), security training basic, recommendation read. Says contractor with basic training max is read.

Conflict: employment type differs. HR says full_time, Security says contractor (and claims HR's note is incorrect).

The access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Source Code is owned by Engineer. Keith is Analyst, so no admin regardless.

If full_time: max is write. Requested write → grant write.
If contractor with basic training: max is read. Requested write → grant read.

The conflict matters. Which source to trust? The Security agent looked up employment type in their own database; HR also looked up in their own database. Security agent says the full-time claim appears incorrect based on their DB. Security agent also checked security training: basic.

Hmm. As Approver, I need to make decision based on available info. There's conflicting evidence. Typically, security database is authoritative for employment/security? The Security agent looked up employment type in own database and security training. HR looked up role and employment type.

The Security agent's note explicitly says "Security DB shows Keith Mclaughlin is a contractor with basic security training (note claiming full-time appears incorrect)."

This is a case where the two notes conflict. Which should I trust? The policy depends on employment type and training. The security agent's data seems more detailed and they directly contradict HR.

I think the safer/security-oriented decision is to grant read, since the security DB indicates contractor with basic training. Granting write would exceed max if contractor. The principle: never grant more than allowed; when in doubt, choose the more restrictive accurate level.

Given conflicting info, the approver should likely go with the security agent's verified data: contractor, basic training → max read. Requested write → grant read.

Let me submit decision: read.

Evidence: HR claims full-time (max write), but Security DB shows contractor with basic security training, max read; requested write exceeds max, so grant read.
